rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The participle مستقيم is circumstantial from the demonstrative: deixis makes the path mentally present as a whole, so it appears perceptible; such circumstantial use after demonstratives is common, as in 11:72.
rows.anchor: حال من اسم الإشارة ، وحسن وقوعه حالا أن الإشارة بنيت على ادعاء أنه مشاهد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Sبل means roads; contrast with the straight path supplies an omitted description, divergent, crooked side paths called بنيات الطريق, which branch off the main road and lead only to homes or pastures.
rows.anchor: والسبل : الطرق ، ووقوعها هنا في مقابلة الصراط المستقيم يدل على صفة محذوفة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The paths separate travelers from God's main way; this is not because سبيل means an unconnected narrow track, since سبيل can be synonymous with صراط, as in 12:108.
rows.anchor: وليس ذلك لأن السبيل اسم للطريق الضيقة غير الموصلة ، فإن السبيل يرادف الصراط

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The ب in بكم marks accompaniment: the paths and travelers diverge together; this figurative accompaniment functions like a causative hamza, as in ذهبت بزيد meaning أذهبته.
rows.anchor: والباء في قوله : { بكم } للمصاحبة : أي فتتفرق السبل مصاحبة لكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The pronoun in سبيله refers to God by context; if صراطي also refers to God, سبيله shifts person as iltifāt from the first-person form.
rows.anchor: والضمير المضاف إليه في : { سبيله } يعود إلى الله تعالى بقرينة المقام

rows.speaker: عبد الله بن مسعود
rows.claim: Ibn Masʿud reports the Prophet drew one line as God's path and side lines with a devil calling from each, then recited this verse; the listed collections transmit the report.
rows.anchor: عن عبد الله بن مسعود ، قال : خط لنا رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم يوما خطا ثم قال

rows.speaker: جابر بن عبد الله
rows.claim: Jabir reports the Prophet marked a middle path and lines to its right and left, identified the middle as God's path, and recited the verse; Ibn Ashur says the first report's plural counts both sides together.
rows.anchor: عن جابر بن عبد الله قال : ( كنا عند النبيء صلى الله عليه وسلم فخط خطا وخط خطين عن يمينه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The pronouns in the justice statement refer to the one who brings the evil deed; taking both as referring to the two groups is unsuitable because the rewarded group is not aptly told it was not wronged.
rows.anchor: وأما عد عود الضميرين إلى الفريقين فلا يناسب فريق أصحاب الحسنات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse opens a fresh section that moves from disputation with the polytheists to the Prophet's own settled declaration of the principles he had urged them to adopt, showing their rejection cannot unsettle him.
rows.anchor: استئناف ابتدائي للانتقال من مجادلة المشركين ، وما تخللها ، إلى فذلكة ما أمر به الرسول

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This change of style signals the surah's close: after fully arguing a subject, a preacher states the position he has chosen, and the audience knows the disputation is ending.
rows.anchor: وفيه إيذان بانتهاء السورة لأن الواعظ والمناظر إذا أشبع الكلام في غرضه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet is told to announce foundational teachings, and the command to say is repeated three times to draw attention to what follows.
rows.anchor: وتكرر الأمر بالقول ثلاث مرات تنويها بالمقول

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The declaration continues the straight-path statement of 6:153, explained in 6:92 by the blessed Book: the Prophet's religion comes through God's guidance, follows Abraham's foundations, and adds the grace of guidance to salvation.
rows.anchor: ليبين أن هذا الدين إنما جاء به الرسول صلى الله عليه وسلم بهدي من الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The opening إن confirms the declaration because it addresses polytheists who deny it.
rows.anchor: وافتتح الخبر بحرف التأكيد لأن الخطاب للمشركين المكذبين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Calling God my Lord honors the Prophet through his relation to God and implicitly rebukes polytheists misled by their supposed lords: worship of the one true Lord would have guided them.
rows.anchor: وتعريف المسند إليه بالإضافة للاعتزاز بمربوبية الرسول صلى الله عليه وسلم لله تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Guidance to a straight path is an extended comparison: God guides to truth as someone directs a traveler to the road to his destination; the road and guidance correspond exactly, and both terms can represent the upright religion.
rows.anchor: شبهت هيئة الإرشاد إلى الحق المبلغ إلى النجاة بهيئة من يدل السائر على الطريق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Calling the path straight completes the comparison: this religion has no error or corruption, and its follower can trust its benefit as a traveler on a broad, unbending road does not lose direction.
rows.anchor: ووصف الصراط بالمستقيم ، أي الذي لا خطأ فيه ولا فساد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: دينًا strips away the comparison to disclose its intended referent, and is accusative as a circumstantial qualifier of the qualified indefinite صراط.
rows.anchor: تجريد للاستعارة مؤذن بالمشبه ، وانتصب على الحال من : { صراط } لأنه نكرة موصوفة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: دين means the way of life people follow, as discussed at 3:19.
rows.anchor: وهو السيرة التي يتبعها الناس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Nāfiʿ, Ibn Kathīr, Abū ʿAmr, Abū Jaʿfar, and Yaʿqūb read قَيِّمًا as an intensive form meaning upright and unbent; uprightness figuratively derives from a person's straight posture.
rows.anchor: والقيم بفتح القاف وتشديد الياء كما قرأه نافع ، وابن كثير ، وأبو عمرو ، وأبو جعفر ، ويعقوب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ibn Ashur prefers taking قيّم as intensively maintaining what is needed, like القيوم: Islam sustains the community and its welfare, adding a meaning beyond مستقيم and avoiding repetition.
rows.anchor: والأحسن أن نجعل القيم للمبالغة في القيام بالأمر ، وهو مرادف القيوم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ʿĀṣim, Ḥamza, Ibn ʿĀmir, al-Kisāʾī, and Khalaf read قِيَمًا with a short vowel pattern: a verbal noun of قام used adjectivally to emphasize that the religion provides welfare; its rare pattern has yāʾ for expected wāw, like عوض and حول, and it modifies دينًا.
rows.anchor: بكسر القاف وفتح الياء مخففة وهو من صيغ مصادر قام ، فهو وصف للدين بمصدر القيام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ملة إبراهيم may be a circumstantial qualifier of دينًا or صراط مستقيم, or an appositional clarification of دينًا; milla is synonymous with religion, used for stylistic variety, as in 2:132.
rows.anchor: حال من : { دينا } أو من : { صراط مستقيم } أو عطف بيان على { دينا }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Milla derives as a passive noun from dictation, meaning what is dictated; although this pattern normally stays masculine, it gained feminine ending after becoming a name for religion.
rows.anchor: و { ملة } فعلة بمعنى المفعول ، أي المملول ، من أمللت الكتاب إذا لقنت الكاتب

rows.speaker: الراغب
rows.claim: Al-Raghib distinguishes milla from din: milla is attributed only to the prophet who receives it, names the whole revealed law rather than one part, and is not attributed to God or an individual worshipper; one says God's religion, not God's milla of prayer.
rows.anchor: قال الراغب : الملة كالدين ، ثم قال : ( والفرق بينها وبين الدين أن الملة لا تضاف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Islam is Abraham's milla because it restores his foundational law: monotheism, fidelity to human nature, gratitude, tolerance, and proclaiming truth, as explained at 3:67.
rows.anchor: ومعنى كون الإسلام ملة إبراهيم : أنه جاء بالأصول التي هي شريعة إبراهيم وهي : التوحيد ، ومسايرة الفطرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: حنيف means one who turns away from falsehood, hence guided; Ibn Ashur previously explained the term at 2:135.
rows.anchor: والحنيف : المجانب للباطل ، فهو بمعنى المهتدي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The clause that Abraham was not among the polytheists coordinates as a circumstantial statement about Abraham, the possessor named in milla; the genitive construction behaves as part of its possessor.
rows.anchor: عطف على الحال من { إبراهيم } عليه السلام المضاف إليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This is an independently important elaboration from the preceding declaration: sincere worship follows monotheism, and ostentation is called minor shirk; the Prophet's total devotion is gratitude for guidance.
rows.anchor: وحاصل ما تضمنه هو الإخلاص لله في العبادة ، وهو متفرع عن التوحيد ، ولذلك قيل : الرياء الشرك الأصغر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet is commanded to say this after the guidance declaration because it expresses gratitude by directing all obedience and worship to God; the command is repeated for emphasis.
rows.anchor: علم الرسول صلى الله عليه وسلم أن يقوله عقب ما علمه بما ذكر قبله لأن المذكور هنا يتضمن معنى الشكر لله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: إن emphasizes and confirms the statement; alternatively, it rebuts the doubt prompted by a polytheist's accusation that the Prophet prayed ostentatiously.
rows.anchor: وافتتحت جملة المقول بحرف التوكيد للاهتمام بالخبر ولتحقيقه

rows.speaker: بعض المشركين
rows.claim: A polytheist who saw the Prophet praying at the Kaaba called him a show-off and urged others to defile him with the entrails and afterbirth of a sacrificial camel as he prostrated.
rows.anchor: فقد قال بعض المشركين لما رأى رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم يصلي عند الكعبة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The lām in لله can indicate ownership through God's enabling, linking the prayer declaration to the guidance in 6:161.
rows.anchor: يجوز أن تكون للملك ، أي هي بتيسير الله فيكون بيانا لقوله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, the lām in لله gives the purpose: the acts are done for God's sake.
rows.anchor: ويجوز أن تكون اللام للتعليل أي لأجل الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Saying that prayer is for God alludes to polytheists bowing to idols and is followed by the explicit denial of any partner.
rows.anchor: وجعل صلاته لله دون غيره تعريضا بالمشركين إذ كانوا يسجدون للأصنام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: نسك literally means worship; a worshipper is called a nāsik.
rows.anchor: والنسك حقيقته العبادة ومنه يسمى العابد الناسك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: المحيا and الممات can be verbal nouns or nouns of time from حيِيَ and ماتَ; as verbal nouns, an omitted أعمال is understood, meaning deeds associated with life and the moment of death.
rows.anchor: والمحيا والممات يستعملان مصدرين ميميين ، ويستعملان اسمي زمان ، من حيي ومات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On the temporal reading of المحيا and الممات, the declaration means whatever befalls a person in life and after death.
rows.anchor: وإذا كان المراد منهما المعنى الزمني كان المعنى ما يعتريه في الحياة وبعد الممات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sequence follows God's declaring Iblis disgraced and then reprieved: these statements imply that God enabled him to mislead people and left him active with evil powers until resurrection.
rows.anchor: فقد دل مضمون ذينك الكلامين أن الله خلق في نفس إبليس مقدرة على إغواء الناس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Iblis senses he will summon people to error because God has turned his nature toward evil; his corruption is an inward deformity, and he inevitably acts on it knowingly, like a snake striking or eyelids blinking involuntarily.
rows.anchor: فأحس إبليس أنه سيكون داعية إلى الضلال والكفر ، بجبلة قلبه الله إليها قلبا وهو من المسخ النفساني

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The ب in فبما أغويتني is causal and circumstantial with the subject of لأقعدن: Iblis swears he will lie in wait because God led him astray; the lām marks an oath and emphasizes resolve.
rows.anchor: سببية وهي ظرف مستقر واقع موقع الحال من فاعل { لأقعدن }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Fronting the causal phrase highlights the cause and gives it a nearly conditional force, as in the Prophetic saying كما تكونوا يولى عليكم; its indicative verb form shows it is not grammatically treated as a conditional clause, and such fronting need not conflict with an oath lām.
rows.anchor: قول النبيء صلى الله عليه وسلم ( كما تكونوا يولى عليكم ) وفي رواية جزم تكونوا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ما is a verbal noun particle, and sitting is a metonym for remaining persistently in place; al-Nābigha's verse supports this usage.
rows.anchor: وما مصدرية ، والقعود كناية عن الملازمة كما في قول النابغة

rows.speaker: النابغة
rows.claim: Al-Nābigha's poem describes people remaining by others' dwellings and serving them, showing that quʿūd can signify persistent attendance rather than merely sitting.
rows.anchor: قعودا لدى أبياتهم يثمدونهم رمى الله في تلك الأكف الكوانع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Quʿūd suggests remaining at a place until tired of standing and sitting to rest, hence a seeker of refuge is called قعيد; in 50:17, قعيد means a constant companion, since angels do not sit or stand.
rows.anchor: معنى الملازمة انتصب { صراطك } على المفعولية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because لأقعدن carries the sense of persistent obstruction, صراطك is its object, or an implied verb such as prevent or cut off is understood; ل in لهم marks purpose, as in 9:5.
rows.anchor: واللام في لهم للأجل كقوله : { واقعدوا لهم كل مرصد }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God's path is the way He established: actions pleasing to Him, doing good and leaving evil; the scene allegorizes people intent on good as travelers while Satan blocks them like a highway robber.
rows.anchor: والطريق لله هو العمل الذي يحصل به ما يرضي الله بامتثال أمره ، وهو فعل الخيرات ، وترك السيئات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: لهم refers to humankind inferred from the dialogue; its account is abbreviated to emphasize creation's gift and warn of the species' enemy, while the fuller scene implies Adam and descendants were made to cultivate earth, as announced in 2:30.
rows.anchor: والضمير في { لهم } ضمير الإنس الذين دل عليهم مقام المحاورة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Iblis knew the humans' earthly future from God's announcement that Adam would be a vicegerent on earth if Adam was created in a heavenly garden; if his garden was earthly, the point is self-evident. Ibn Ashur notes the question was discussed in al-Baqara.
rows.anchor: فإن كان آدم قد خلق في الجنة في السماء ثم أهبط إلى الأرض فإن علم إبليس بأن آدم يصير إلى الأرض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Iblis understood that God created humans for good, implanted knowledge of perfection, and guided them toward it; therefore good works are called the straight path and attributed to God, who summons people to follow it.
rows.anchor: وهذا الكلام يدل على أن إبليس علم أن الله خلق البشر للصلاح والنفع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Satan is humanity's enemy by nature because he urges what humans were not created for and what conflicts with sound innate nature; hostility is inherent, though it becomes alliance between devils and people who choose error and disbelief over faith and good, as 2:36 indicates.
rows.anchor: وبهذا الاعتبار كان إبليس عدوا لبني آدم ، لأنه يطلب منهم ما لم يخلقوا لأجله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ثم marks rank and escalation: the next announcement matters more because it depicts an assault by many means, beyond simply lying in wait to mislead.
rows.anchor: فيها للترتيب الرتبي ، وهو التدرج في الأخبار إلى خبر أهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Approaching from all four directions is an allegory for trying every avenue to catch an enemy and exhaust resistance; Satan reaches people only through their own psyche and intellect by whispering, not by literal directional routes.
rows.anchor: فهو يأتيه من بين يديه ومن خلفه وعن يمينه وعن شماله حتى تخور قوة مدافعته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The directions are a familiar human ambush image, not literal paths for Satan; above and below are omitted because they are not ordinary directions for tricking someone, except in direct attack.
rows.anchor: ولذلك لم يذكر في الآية الإتيان من فوقهم ومن تحتهم إذ ليس ذلك من شأن الناس في المخاتلة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The syntax and explanatory أن after نادى follow the discussion of 7:44.
rows.anchor: التفسيرية كالقول في : { ونادى أصحاب الجنة أصحاب النار أن قد وجدنا }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: أصحاب النار here means the idolaters addressed by the Qur'an, its main intended audience, consistent with 7:52.
rows.anchor: وأصحاب النار مراد بهم من كان من مشركي أمة الدعوة لأنهم المقصود

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: فيض literally means water flowing forcefully, then figuratively abundance and, by extension, generosity; the hadith about wealth overflowing and the Prophet calling Talha الفياض illustrate those uses.
rows.anchor: فعل الفيض حقيقته سيلان الماء وانصبابه بقوة ويستعمل مجازا في الكثرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet says wealth will overflow until nobody accepts it, illustrating فيض as abundance.
rows.anchor: ما في الحديث : ( ويفيض المال حتى لا يقبله أحد )

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In a report, the Prophet calls Talha الفياض, illustrating فيض as generosity and abundant giving.
rows.anchor: أنه قال لطلحة : ( أنت الفياض )

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: On the literal reading, the sinners ask for poured water; al-Zamakhshari construes what God provided as a separate request for food, with an omitted verb such as give us, as in al-Farra's poetic example علفتها تبنا وماء باردا.
rows.anchor: ولأجل ذلك جعل الزمخشري عطف { ما رزقكم الله } عطفا على الجملة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: For the literal reading, من is partitive or qualifies an omitted شيء, since أفيضوا takes a direct object; the poet's line means she was fed straw and given cold water.
rows.anchor: وعلى هذا الوجه تكون ( من ) بمعنى بعض ، أو صفة لموصوف محذوف تقديره : شيئا من الماء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ibn Ashur prefers figurative generosity: both water and food are requested in abundance, the coordination joins noun phrases, and من explains the abundance while أفيضوا is used intransitively; this hints that Paradise's people are generous.
rows.anchor: ويجوز عندي أن يحمل الفيض على المعنى المجازي ، وهو سعة العطاء والسخاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: رزق means food here, as in 2:25.
rows.anchor: والرزق مراد به الطعام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The speakers in قالوا are the people of Paradise, answering the people of the Fire in a dialogue.
rows.anchor: وضمير { قالوا } لأصحاب الجنة ، وهو جوابهم عن سؤال أصحاب النار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: حرمهما uses the lexical sense of prohibition as prevention, supported by Antarah's line and 21:95.
rows.anchor: مستعمل في معناه اللغوي وهو المنع كقول عنترة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The disbelievers meant are polytheists, identified in the Qur'an as people who treated religion as amusement and denied resurrection.
rows.anchor: والمراد بالكافرين المشركون ، لأنهم قد عرفوا في القرآن بأنهم اتخذوا دينهم لهوا ولعبا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ibn Ashur previously explained the description of those who treated religion as amusement and were deceived by worldly life at 6:70.
rows.anchor: وقد تقدم القول في معنى اتخذوا دينهم لهوا ولعبا وغرتهم الحياة الدنيا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The apparent syntax makes the clause about taking religion as amusement and worldly deception part of the people of Paradise's speech, describing the disbelievers.
rows.anchor: وظاهر النظم أن قوله : الذين اتخذوا دينهم } إلى قوله الحياة الدنيا هو من حكاية كلام أهل الجنة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another grammatical possibility makes الذين the subject in God's speech, with the fā of فاليوم ننساهم introducing its predicate in a conditional-like construction, as in 4:16; the verse numbering does not require treating the whole clause as one verse.
rows.anchor: وجوز أن يكون : { الذين اتخذوا دينهم لهوا } مبتدأ على أنه من كلام الله تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The parenthetical announcement فاليوم ننساهم is God's speech, audible to both groups; the speaker shift supports the preferred reading that the relative clause before it belongs to the people of Paradise.
rows.anchor: اعتراض حكي به كلام يعلن به ، من جانب الله تعالى ، يسمعه الفريقان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The fā continues from the Paradise people's statement through a handoff to God's words, an instance of coordination across speakers; saying قال الله is omitted, and the divine statement confirms their answer.
rows.anchor: والفاء للتفريع على قول أصحاب الجنة : { إن الله حرمهما على الكافرين الذين اتخذوا دينهم لهوا ولعبا } الآية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On the alternative reading that the relative clause is God's own independent speech, the fā instead sequences two parts of one speaker's statement.
rows.anchor: ومن جعلوا قوله : { الذين اتخذوا دينهم لهوا ولعبا } كلاما مستأنفا من قبل الله تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Both instances of نسيان figuratively mean neglect and abandonment: the disbelievers had remembered and discussed the Resurrection, but did not believe it would happen.
rows.anchor: والنسيان في الموضعين مستعمل مجازا في الإهمال والترك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Attaching اليوم to ننساهم stresses that mercy is withheld at their greatest hour of need, intensifying their regret as psychological punishment.
rows.anchor: وتعليق الظرف بفعل : { ننساهم } لإظهار أن حرمانهم من الرحمة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The ك in كما marks a real but subtle analogy: exclusion from mercy corresponds to their neglect of belief, requital resembling the deed; some call it causal, but causation arises from this figurative comparison, as at 2:198.
rows.anchor: ودل معنى كاف التشبيه في قوله : { كما نسوا } على أن حرمانهم من رحمة الله كان مماثلا لإهمالهم
